entries.title: Default Software
entries.subtitle: Baseline for Windows applications rather than games

variants.label: Software defaults
variants.whenToUse: Apply to a bottle used for desktop applications instead of games
rationale: DXVK brings up Direct3D 10/11, which Chromium and Electron shells use for UI acceleration; wined3d cannot on current macOS
D3DMetal takes down Chromium-based apps, so it is avoided for software
Async shader compilation keeps UI interactions from hitching, and its visual-glitch trade-off does not matter for application UIs
Balanced preset: none of the game-oriented shader shortcuts

notes: A general-purpose baseline for running Windows software rather than games.

entries.title: Diagnostics Off
entries.subtitle: Clears every overlay

variants.label: Turn diagnostics off
rationale: Clears the FPS counter, the Metal HUD and the frame-rate logging in one step

notes: Changes only overlays. Graphics backend, sync and performance settings are left alone.

entries.title: Diagnostics On
entries.subtitle: Frame rate and GPU overlays

variants.label: Turn diagnostics on
rationale: The FPS counter follows the active backend: the DXVK HUD where DXVK runs, and Wine's fps debug channel on WineD3D, which has no overlay and logs instead
Metal HUD draws only on Metal backends, so it stays dark on WineD3D

notes: Changes only overlays. Graphics backend, sync and performance settings are left alone.

entries.title: Lineage II
entries.subtitle: L2Gold Essence client

variants.label: WineD3D, tuned
variants.whenToUse: The fastest configuration measured on Apple Silicon
rationale: Measured: wined3d over OpenGL plays fine, while d9vk (D3D9 to Vulkan to MoltenVK) ran below 1 fps
Lineage II is DirectX 9; DXMT and D3DMetal only translate D3D11 and D3D12, so neither can sit in front of it
Performance preset and compatibility mode both switch off Metal validation and event tracking, which Apple’s Metal-backed OpenGL driver still pays for
msync is the cheapest sync primitive on macOS, and fsync is switched off alongside it
The client is 32-bit, so WINE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE lets it address beyond 2 GB in crowded areas

notes: Client installed into the bottle by hand; launches and plays.

Unreal Engine 2 is draw-call bound and Wine taxes every call, so the in-game Option.ini settings matter more than the graphics backend. RENDERCHARACTERCOUNT, PawnShadow and RenderDeco are the expensive ones.

Some private servers ship L2.exe as an Active Anticheat launcher that installs a kernel driver Wine cannot load, with the real game in l2.bin. This client is not one of them: the two files are byte-identical, so no driver is involved.

Every dependency the client needs (D3DX9_40, d3dcompiler_43/47, msxml4, vcomp120) ships in system_en, so no winetricks verbs are required. The embedded Chromium UI needs its sandbox disabled, which Nightcap does for every bottle.

knownIssues.description: d9vk (DXVK d3d9) renders under 1 fps through MoltenVK and is not usable for this game
knownIssues.workaround: Leave the backend on WineD3D; do not install a native d3d9.dll into the bottle
